subject: Re: Ambi <> Encord
text:
Hi Jamie,

Following up with some answers to your questions:

*Platform*

   - Expected number of users to be registered with the Encord platform
   (i.e. admins, ML engineers and annotators)

5-10

   - Expected volumes of data (i.e. number of images, videos w/ average
   length) to go through the Encord platform over the next twelve months.

As I mentioned, our #1 priority is the annotation service and we would look
into the platform only after. That being said, to give some context we have
over 1B images collected over the past 3 years. Unsure if we will migrate
all/some of those into the platform, but it gives you a sense of our yearly
data collection volume.

*Annotation Services*

   - Expected amount of images/frames to be annotated per month/year?

So our volume was a bit lower last year as it was mainly sustaining
engineering of older models - somewhere in the ballpark of 50-60k images.
That being said, a decent chunk of this was "dense" annotations where there
are numerous annotations per image. See tasks below.

This year could be much higher as we look to support next-gen models such
as PRIME-1. That being said, we are still scoping out the next steps on
that front and thus can't concretely say which tasks we will pursue / what
annotations will be required.

   - Task(s) description

The best way to break this down is we have object-centric annotation tasks
and then sparse/dense annotation of individual images.

Tasks:

   - Classification: Classify the object or some properties about it
   - Segmentation: Segment the object

Note that these are often combined - i.e. segment then classify each
segmented polygon.

Sparse/dense:

   - Sparse: You're doing this for 1-3 objects/image
   - Dense: You're doing this for 10-20 objects/image

 Hope this helps. Looking forward to chatting tmrw!

Best,
Vishal

subject: Re: Labeling project
text:
Hi Matt,

I added 5 more videos to show how we caption the segmented motions. In this
labelling project, the 7 categories represent coarse-level action labels,
and the detailed motion descriptions represent the fine-grained motions for
the coarse-level labels.

Regarding the detailed motion description, the principle is to faithfully
describe how the subject does the task. For example, when lifting a box,
the subject can either simply pick up the box from the table without
bending over, or lean forward, stretch his two arms to pick the box up.
These scenarios are very different in our ergonomic assessments so we hope
our model could learn the difference.

Please let me know if you have any questions or concerns. Thanks!

Jun
